header.name: Functional Safety for Safety Critical Systems
header.description:
This course introduces functional safety concepts and industry practices for designing safety-critical electronic systems, with emphasis on semiconductor and SoC design. Students will learn how failures propagate in complex systems such as Battery Managmeent Systems and Traction Inverters and understand how functional safety standards (ISO 26262, IEC 61508) drive architectural and design decisions for Automotive ECUs.

The course then connects system-level safety goals with SoC Architecture decisions - including safety mechanisms in SoCs, diagnostic coverage, fault tolerance, failure-rate analysis, failure prediction through silicon lifecycle management (SLM), and predictive maintenance. The course provides introduction to safety analysis techniques such as FMEDA, DFA, FTA. Interactive lectures, weekly quizzes, case studies, and an end-term exploration/survey project help students bridge conceptual understanding with industry practice.
prerequisites_desirable: ECE516 System on Chip Design and Test
MTH201 Probability and Statistics (helpful for failure-rate topics)

outcomes.label: CO1
outcomes.raw_text: Understand the need for functional safety and its applications. Understand basic concepts and terminology. Apply functional safety concepts and terminology to identify hazards, safety goals, and safe states in safety-critical systems such as automotive ECUs, lifts, battery management systems, and traction inverters.

outcomes.label: CO2
outcomes.raw_text: Analyze fault-tolerant architectures, failure modes, failure rates, and diagnostic coverage to evaluate whether a proposed system or SoC design meets specified safety requirements

outcomes.label: CO3
outcomes.raw_text: Evaluate SoC-level safety mechanisms - including redundancy, monitoring, error detection/correction, and silicon lifecycle management - for their effectiveness in meeting functional safety objectives in a chosen application domain.

lecture_topics: Safety and its types
Introduction to Functional Safety and its applications
risk
risk assessment
malfunction and failures (failure types - systematic and random)
Risk Mitigation techniques and fault avoidance techniques
Introduction to Safety Standards and product development process
Battery Management System: Identification of Hazards, Risk, Safety Goal definition, Safe States
Mapping Safety Goals to Functional Safety Requirements at System Level
Traction Inverter System: Identification of Hazards, Risk, Safety Goal definition, Safe States
Mapping Safety Goals to Functional Safety Requirements at System Level
Introduction to Fail Safe, Fail Operational, Fail Silent and availability
Deriving SoC Safety Architecture from System Safety Architecture
Concept of Safety Element out of Context
Safety Island in an SoC

SoC Safety Mechanisms and diagnostic coverage: Watchdog, voltage/clock/temperature monitors, Memory protection - ECC/Parity, Interconnect Protection, CRC, Lockstep, Redundancy, Protection over communication channels (CAN, Ethernet, etc.), BIST
Safety Metrics and their calculation for Automotive SoCs: Failure Rate Prediction, Single Point Metric, Latent Fault Metric, FMEDA introduction
Design Needs of a Safety SoC: Development process, Fault Injection, Requirements from ISO 26262
Introduction to Safety Analysis beyond FMEDA - FMEA, FTA, DFA
Special Topics: Silicon Lifecycle Management, Predictive Maintenance and related VLSI circuits
